newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility falls after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility falls after U.S. data.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options eased off on Friday after the release of U.S. consumer price data, traders said.
August U.S. CPI rose 0.1 percent in the overall and the core rate, less than the 0.2 percent rise expected.
December options straddles on the December futures contract were trading at a volatility of 19 percent, after starting the day around 20 percent.
"A lot of the locals bought back shorts after the data," said a broker at a U.S. house in London. "There was also some interest in December 96.75 calls."
December Euromark futures were up two basis points at 96.81 by 1431 GMT.
About 3,600 calls were traded at the 96.75 strike in December with a further 1,450 at the 97.00 strike. A major British house sold 1,000 call spreads at 96.75, traders said.
"There's been a lot of buying all week of the 97.00 calls from market-makers," said a broker at a British securities firm. "It's been the strike with the heaviest trading this week."
He said part of the volume had resulted from investors rolling-over positions into March, by selling two December 97.00 calls to buy one March 97.00 call.
Around 1,700 calls were traded at the March 97.00 strike, and more than 1,000 at the 96.50 strike.
The U.S. broker said volatility of March calls had slipped to around 17.25 percent from around 18 percent earlier.
The British broker said volatility was starting to look cheap at these levels, and would rise in the next week.
Elsewhere, December short sterling volatility was pushed down sharply by paper and local selling.
It fell to 8.5 to 9.7 percent from 9.8 to 10.6 percent earlier in the day, brokers said. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6137
